title: The Art of Double Meaning
text:
Puns exploit the fact that a single word can carry two distinct meanings at once, and skilled writers use this ambiguity to surprise their readers. A headline such as 'Bank Closes Doors After Robbery' may amuse precisely because it invites two incompatible readings. Far from being trivial, such wordplay often reveals how deeply language is shaped by context and expectation. Linguists therefore study puns not as jokes alone but as evidence of how the mind resolves ambiguity.

However, the same ambiguity that delights an audience can also mislead it. Advertisers and politicians sometimes deploy double meanings deliberately, allowing listeners to hear the message they prefer while retaining a defence if challenged. Translators face an even greater difficulty, because a pun that works in one language usually collapses in another. Consequently, a successful translation often sacrifices the joke in order to preserve the underlying meaning.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does a pun exploit?
options: The fact that one word can carry two distinct meanings at once
The loud pronunciation of certain consonants
The strict grammar of formal headlines
The shortness of a typical sentence

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what difficulty do translators face?
options: A pun that works in one language usually collapses in another
Dictionaries do not include enough nouns
Readers refuse to accept any joke
Their pay is always lower than advertisers

questions.text: Why might linguists treat puns as more than simple jokes?
options: Because they reveal how the mind resolves ambiguity
Because puns are always written by scientists
Because jokes are forbidden in academic writing
Because puns never depend on context

questions.text: What does the author imply about deliberate double meanings in advertising and politics?
options: They can allow the speaker to avoid responsibility if challenged
They are always harmless entertainment for audiences
They are rarely noticed by listeners at all
They are banned by law in every country

vocabulary.definition: the quality of having more than one possible meaning
the circumstances in which something happens or is said
gives up something valuable in order to achieve another goal

paragraph_translations: Żarty słowne wykorzystują fakt, że pojedyncze słowo może jednocześnie nieść dwa różne znaczenia, a wprawni pisarze używają tej wieloznaczności, by zaskoczyć czytelnika. Nagłówek w rodzaju 'Bank zamyka drzwi po napadzie' może bawić właśnie dlatego, że zaprasza do dwóch wykluczających się odczytań. Daleko mu do banalności, bo tego rodzaju gra słowna często ujawnia, jak głęboko język kształtuje kontekst i oczekiwania. Lingwiści badają więc żarty słowne nie tylko jako dowcip, lecz jako dowód na to, jak umysł rozstrzyga niejednoznaczność.

Ta sama wieloznaczność, która bawi publiczność, może jednak także wprowadzać ją w błąd. Reklamodawcy i politycy czasem celowo stosują podwójne znaczenia, pozwalając słuchaczom usłyszeć to, co im najbardziej odpowiada, i zachowując jednocześnie możliwość obrony w razie krytyki. Tłumacze mierzą się z jeszcze większym problemem, ponieważ żart działający w jednym języku zwykle rozpada się w innym. W efekcie udane tłumaczenie często poświęca dowcip, by zachować podstawowe znaczenie.
